title: Volume 1 Chapter 5: Failed Experiment
content: In the storage facility rented by the development team, I was explaining the events at the academy to Dr. Smith and Dr. Alison. I had already sent a message about the situation earlier, but I needed to answer their questions for more details.
"That concludes my report," I said.
After finishing my explanation, Dr. Smith placed a hand on his forehead, looking troubled, but he didn’t seem to feel any sense of crisis.
"I never expected the academy's female students to find out. I had Alison tell the truth, thinking it would lead to aversion, which is why I made it classified information," he said.
For Dr. Smith, it seemed that it was merely a matter of making his experiments more difficult. In contrast, Dr. Alison wore a serious expression.
"If information has leaked, the most suspicious person is the principal. She requested the disclosure of our information as a condition for providing the academy's facilities," she stated.
Dr. Smith didn’t seem particularly interested and appeared to have no intention of figuring out who leaked the information.
"We signed a non-disclosure agreement, didn’t we? In that case, the principal shouldn’t be the one," he replied.
Dr. Alison looked exasperated at Dr. Smith's lack of suspicion towards the principal.
"...Sigh. This means they see us as nothing more than that. Anyway, I’ll go confirm with the principal," she said, leaving the storage facility.
Dr. Smith waved her off casually.
"Take care."
I felt uneasy about Dr. Smith's lack of tension.
"Even with the information leak, you seem as relaxed as ever, Dr. Smith."
"For me, it’s finally time for the long-awaited experiment. The preparations will be done the day after tomorrow, so right now, focusing on the experiment is more important."
"The experiment with the Magic Power Converter, right?"
No matter how well the Thunderbolt, a humanoid weapon, moved, it wouldn’t be of any use against Gijuu unless the Magic Power Converter was activated to generate a force field.

"We’ve confirmed that magic power is being generated from your limbs, internal organs, and left eye. The only thing left is to see if it can be used at a combat level," Dr. Smith said, beaming as he lightly patted my back.
"I’m looking forward to it, Ichinose-kun."
I straightened my posture and replied, "I will do my utmost, albeit with limited power."
"...You’re still so stiff. Can’t you be a bit more casual? My shoulders are getting tense just being around you."
"If you want, I can give you a shoulder massage."
"Huh? Really? Then maybe I’ll take you up on that. I’ve been busy with preparations lately."
In the principal's office, Alison was pressing Principal Kase about the information leak.
"Weren’t we supposed to have signed a non-disclosure agreement? I would like an explanation as to how our confidential information reached the female students," she demanded.

From Alison’s perspective, it was nothing short of a condescending act. She was in a position to corner the academy with the contract, so she took a strong stance. However, Principal Kase showed no signs of being flustered.
She calmly reviewed documents and signed her name, treating it as a task to be completed alongside her other work.
"Do you have any evidence that I leaked it?" she asked.
"The only ones who know the secrets at the academy are us and you," Alison replied.
"Isn’t it possible that someone from the development team leaked it?"
"Are you joking? The most likely suspect is you."
Alison had several reasons for not suspecting the development team.

One was that the members of the development team had limited contact with the female students. The only exception was Ren, but she couldn’t imagine him leaking information. For better or worse, Hifumi Ren was a soldier.

The second reason was that one of the conditions for participating in the Prometheus Project was that, aside from those like Dr. Smith and Ren, only those dissatisfied with the current situation were allowed to join. Many were unable to tolerate Valkyries wielding power within the organization.
Principal Kase sighed softly and looked at Alison. Once a fierce warrior who survived brutal battlefields as a Valkyrie, her gaze made Alison flinch slightly.
"I swear, I have not leaked any information. If I did, it would hinder the children’s opportunities to interact with men."
"Then why?!"
As Alison raised her voice to avoid being intimidated, Principal Kase responded.
"We will conduct our investigation as well. You should return and investigate your own team. —That’s all. You may leave."
The final words were delivered coldly, making it clear that she had no intention of continuing the conversation.
Clenching her jaw, Alison left the principal's office.
Tomorrow marks the start of the full-scale experiment.
Currently, I could only train, but today I took extra time to prepare thoroughly. As a result, my steps felt unsteady now. I was exhausted to the point where walking felt like a chore.
"If I succeed, it will lead to the next step. I must succeed without fail."
Determined to achieve the success that defined my existence, I aimed to get to my room early tonight.
The path from the storage facility to my room was dimly lit. Since I had gotten back later than usual, I should have brought a flashlight. That was my mistake.
"Hm? Is something the matter?"
As I stopped on the dark path, I noticed a figure peeking out from behind a container.
As my eyes adjusted, I could see that the person was wearing a red cloak.
It seemed they were surprised that I noticed them.
"You noticed me even though I was hiding," the person said confidently, showing no sign of fear.
The ace of the Boots Cat, Hayase Maya, stepped forward, approaching me.
"I never thought you would be participating in such a ridiculous experiment," she stated directly.
Caught off guard by her straightforward question, I hesitated slightly.
"...I cannot answer that as it pertains to confidential matters."
"That’s the same as answering. I was wondering what a man was doing sneaking into the academy, and it turns out you’re trying to imitate a Valkyrie?"
I had anticipated direct interference since the last attack, but I never expected her to approach me. Remembering Louise’s words, I couldn’t help but be wary of Hayase-san.
"I am a test pilot and am not in a position to discuss the experiment. Excuse me."
As I tried to walk away, she matched my pace beside me.
When I attempted to quicken my steps, she laughed.
"I’m good at running too. Want to give it a try? You seem pretty tired over there."
After training to my limits, I had no energy left to race against her.
I resigned myself to walking beside her and decided to maintain my silence, refusing to answer her questions.
She began talking on her own.
"If the information I’ve heard is correct, you’re participating in an inhumane experiment, right? The idea of creating limbs from Gijuu cells is absurd."
I remained silent in response to her criticism of the experiment.
She continued to speak, ignoring my silence.
"Why did you join the experiment?"
"Oh, you won’t answer? Then how about I say it’s a direct order from a superior? I’m a lieutenant, after all. You’re a warrant officer, right? Is it okay to defy a superior?"
Hayase-san, no, Lieutenant Hayase lightly tapped her rank insignia with her fingertip and laughed.
I hadn’t noticed due to the unique rank insignia used at the academy, but I was surprised to find that she was two ranks above me.
Louise also referred to her as Hayase-san, treating her as an equal... No, that was just an excuse.
Even if she wasn’t my direct superior, I was showing a lack of respect.
"Ah!? I apologize for my previous rudeness. However, I cannot speak about the project. Please understand, Lieutenant."
As I stopped and saluted, she laughed, holding her stomach.
"Ahahaha! You really are serious, aren’t you? I’m surprised you actually stopped ignoring me just because of your rank."
"...Are you mocking me?"
If Louise was correct, she was the one who would interfere with the Prometheus Project.
Noticing my growing wariness, her smile faded.
"Yes, I am mocking you. I thought I’d give you a warning to stop participating in this ridiculous project."
Her words about the "ridiculous project" might have been intended as provocation.
I reminded myself that if I responded angrily, I would be playing into her hands, so I resolved to remain calm.
"I appreciate your advice. However, for me, continuing with the project is my very reason for existence. Moreover, I have no right to withdraw from the project."
She frowned at my attitude and shot me a sharp look.
"...What’s that supposed to mean?"
Her voice was lower than before, tinged with anger.
She turned her back to me and walked away.
"I wasted my concern on you."
Her attitude suggested she had lost interest in me, which I found somewhat relieving.
However, I couldn’t help but wonder what had caused her sudden change in demeanor.
The day of the experiment had finally arrived.
Although it was a weekday, I had contacted the academy to inform them I would be absent to prioritize the experiment.
I changed into my pilot suit and waited in the cockpit.
"This is Envy; we will now begin the test of the Magic Power Converter."
Dr. Smith’s face appeared on the cockpit monitor.
"Do you remember the manual?"
"Yes."
The materials related to the experiment were extensive, but I had read through them all by today.
"Good. However, there are some changes, so I will explain them."
Was it too greedy to wish I had been informed in advance?
Dr. Smith was brilliant, but he often made such mistakes.
It was understandable why Dr. Alison frequently sighed while looking after him.
"The magic power you generate will flow through the control stick and foot pedals to the Magic Power Converter. From there, it will efficiently distribute magic power throughout the entire machine."
The Thunderbolt—a humanoid weapon—was about five meters tall.
It was roughly twice the size of a Valkyrie’s battle dress, and the amount of magic power used was also expected to increase, according to the researchers.
Thus, the Magic Power Converter installed in the Thunderbolt was superior to those in the Valkyries’ battle dresses, at least in terms of performance.
The reason for not preparing a male battle dress for this experiment was partly due to the issue of the Magic Power Converter's size.
"If we set the limit of the converter at one hundred percent, the output we expect from you is... about ten percent? That should barely allow for combat."
Hearing that the target was one-tenth of the limit, I naturally tightened my grip on the control stick.
"Understood!"
"Good response. Now, let’s begin the experiment. Start supplying magic power."
"Yes!"
I focused on the limbs I had attached and began releasing magic power.
The Gijuu limbs emitted a faint light, and magic power flowed from them through the control stick into the machine.
I could hear Dr. Alison’s voice through the communicator.
"What is this!?"
Around the Thunderbolt, numerous measuring devices were prepared.
The development staff were each glued to their measuring instruments, measuring the magic power flowing through the cables connected to the Thunderbolt.
"We cannot confirm the generation of a force field in the right forearm."
"In the left leg... we can barely confirm the generation of a force field."
"We confirmed the generation of a force field in the chest, but... it hasn’t reached the required value."
Reports came in one after another, but none of them yielded the desired results.
Alison had expected this outcome, but facing it as reality was painful.
"Indeed, we didn’t reach the required value. I thought there would be a difference between genders, but even after transplanting limbs, a heart, and the left eye, we get this result?"
Alison’s gaze turned to Dr. Smith, but he showed no signs of panic despite being confronted with the failure of the experiment.

"I had heard that men are not suited for handling magic power, but if it’s this different, it’s going to be tough. It might be faster to replace everything below the neck with Gijuu parts. No, how about transplanting a brain? What do you think about transplanting a brain into a body made from Gijuu cells? I think Envy could handle it, but what’s your opinion, Alison?"
His eyes sparkled with excitement, looking almost childlike in his innocent enjoyment.
That only served to highlight Dr. Smith’s abnormality.
"...Even just the limbs involved considerable pain during surgery. I don’t think it would succeed."
Alison chose her words carefully in response.
She had a strong conviction that if she said there was a possibility, the man in front of her would proceed without hesitation.
Dr. Smith hung his head.
"Looks like it’s no good. In that case, let’s replace the remaining left arm and right leg with new ones... Yeah, that’s within the margin of error for our objectives."
As Alison reviewed the aggregated results, she asked Dr. Smith about future experiments.
"At this point, we cannot protect the machine with a force field, and supplying magic power to the weapons is also at an impossible level."
"How about equipping a magic power storage battery?"
"I wouldn’t recommend it since it’s larger and less efficient than the converter. You know why it’s not included in the Valkyrie’s Valkyrie Dress, right?"

The idea of a magic power storage battery had been considered by the organization, but when they tried to develop it, it turned out to be larger and had insufficient storage capacity, rendering it useless.
"In that case, we’re at an impasse. While we have Envy do his best, we should focus on adjusting the converter and reviewing the machine."
Dr. Smith shifted his thoughts and seemed to be ready to delve into machine adjustments.
Alison muttered under her breath so that no one could hear.
"Do your best... huh? No one knows what to do to make that happen, yet you say it so easily."
Dr. Smith had a likable demeanor, but inside, he was a scientist who didn’t care about others.
That’s why he could easily arrive at the idea of extracting Ren’s brain.
He was willing to use even Hifumi Ren, a precious success story, without hesitation.
(Despite surviving a grueling surgery, it seems I will eventually be killed by Dr. Smith. Not dying during the surgery might have been an unfortunate twist of fate.)
After letting out a small sigh, Alison communicated with Ren.
"Envy, the experiment is canceled."
"Canceled? Did we not reach the required value?"
"We didn’t even reach one percent. ...The result is a failure."
I could have softened my words, but Alison chose to speak coldly.
She held no affection for the experimental subject.
The expression on Ren’s face, reflected on the small monitor, seemed to show shock even to Alison.
(So he can make that kind of face... Hm? Just now, did his magic power output slightly increase...? No, it must be my imagination.)
Judging that any increase in output was still within the margin of error, Alison said to Ren, "Come down. I will explain what’s next."
"Understood... I will."
